fields.rationale: States cluster around whether they rely purely on substantial equivalency (SE), offer SE as the primary path with a traditional fallback (exam + 4yr experience), use older traditional reciprocity criteria, emphasize practice privileges for out-of-state CPAs, or frame the process primarily as endorsement based on good standing.

assignments.raw_value: Applicant must have passed the Uniform CPA Examination for their initial license, meet board-established accounting experience requirements, not be subject to pending disciplinary proceedings in another state, and be of good moral character.

Holder of a valid CPA certificate from another state with substantially equivalent qualifications; may waive exam. CPAs from other jurisdictions transferring into Alabama must obtain an Alabama reciprocal certificate within 24 months.

Applicant must have passed the exam with passing grades, meets current AR requirements or met them at time of issuance, has required experience, and has fulfilled continuing education requirements. Alternatively, substantial equivalency via NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service. Also available for holders of foreign designations under § 17-12-308(c).

Applicant must have a certificate, registration or license from another jurisdiction with substantially equivalent requirements, or meet alternative experience/education criteria. May also qualify if employed as CPA for 10 of 15 preceding years.

Applicant must hold a current, active, and unrestricted CPA license from another state with comparable licensure requirements; must not have committed acts or crimes constituting grounds for denial under Section 480; to sign attest reports must meet experience requirements of Section 5095.

Applicant must satisfy the requirements of the occupational credential portability program under section 12-20-202(3), which requires substantially equivalent credentials or at least one year of valid licensure in another jurisdiction with substantially similar scope of practice.

Out-of-state CPAs with a valid CPA license from a substantially equivalent state (as verified by NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service) may practice without obtaining a CT license; no notice, fee, or other submission required. Alternatively, individual CPA qualifications may be verified as substantially equivalent by NASBA. Consent to CT board jurisdiction and other conditions required.

Applicant must have passed the Uniform CPA Examination and hold a valid CPA certificate, license or permit in a substantially equivalent state, or individually be determined substantially equivalent. Non-equivalent applicants must show: passed Uniform CPA Examination; 4 years of relevant experience within the 10 years preceding application; and fulfilled applicable CPE requirements if certificate was issued more than 4 years prior.

Licensure by endorsement available to: (1) unlicensed applicants meeting FL education/experience/character requirements who passed a substantially equivalent exam; (2) holders of valid out-of-state licenses where criteria were substantially equivalent; (3) holders with 10+ years of licensure who passed a substantially equivalent exam. Out-of-state CPAs without FL office may practice under practice privilege if their state has substantially equivalent standards.

Applicant must hold a CPA certificate from another state issued after an equivalent examination; reciprocal privileges must be extended to Georgia citizens by that other state; exam waived for applicants with 10 years of public practice in another state

Holds, and has continued to hold, a valid comparable certificate, registration, or license of certified public accountant of another state for not less than ten years and has been in active practice for not less than five years; or passed the Uniform CPA Examination in another state.

Must hold a valid certificate or license in good standing in another state and meet one of: (a) substantially equivalent state standards, (b) substantially equivalent individual qualifications, or (c) passed equivalent exam, four years of experience within ten years preceding application, and if certificate issued more than four years prior, fulfillment of CPE requirements.

Applicant must be 18+, of good character, have obtained the education and passed the uniform CPA examination with standards no less than those required in Idaho, and have completed the necessary experience, CPE, and board-approved ethics examination required for Idaho licensure. These requirements are waived if the applicant has been licensed as a CPA for no less than 4 years within the 10 years immediately preceding the application.

Must hold a current, valid, unrevoked CPA license from another state with equivalent educational requirements and examination standards; applicant must possess qualifications substantially equivalent to Illinois' current licensing requirements, or at time of original licensure, or have 4+ years of experience within the 10 years preceding the application.

Reciprocity available via: (1) substantial equivalency — board determines individual's CPA qualifications are substantially equivalent to Indiana's requirements; or (2) traditional reciprocity — passed exam, had 4 years of experience in Indiana or another state within the past 10 years, and met CPE requirements. Out-of-state CPAs whose home state is substantially equivalent may practice in Indiana without obtaining a certificate (practice privilege).

Board may waive examination and issue certificate to out-of-state CPA who either passed exam with grades that would have been passing in Kansas and meets current/historical requirements or had 4 years of qualifying experience within last 10 years, or meets substantial equivalency standard. Out-of-state CPAs meeting substantial equivalency may also exercise practice privileges without obtaining a Kansas permit.

Applicant must satisfy educational requirement (KRS 325.261(3)), receive a passing grade on the Uniform CPA Examination equivalent to KY passing grade, hold a valid active CPA license in good standing from another state, and meet current experience requirements or have had 4 years of experience within the preceding 10 years.

Substantial equivalency: the board or its designee must verify that the applicant's education, examination, and experience requirements are comparable to or exceed Louisiana's requirements. Alternatively, a certificate holder from another state may obtain a certificate upon showing passing grades on the Uniform CPA exam, four years of qualifying experience within the preceding ten years, and, if the certificate was issued more than four years prior, fulfillment of Louisiana's CPE requirements.

Applicant must have passed the CPA exam with grades that would have been passing in Massachusetts, and either meet all current MA requirements, or met MA requirements at time of their certificate issuance, or had 4 years of experience in public accountancy within the prior 10 years.

Applicant must be of good character, at least 18 years old, pay fees, and provide adequate evidence of substantially equivalent education, examination, and experience requirements. Substantial equivalency may also be established through NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service or by passing the Uniform CPA Exam and obtaining 4 years of practical work experience within the last 10 years.
Licensure by substantial equivalency (via NASBA verification) or by meeting current Maine requirements; also licensure by endorsement process established under 32 §12231-A.

Applicant must hold a valid and unrevoked CPA certificate from another state or US jurisdiction and either (a) show original certificate was based on equivalent standards, or (b) have 4 years of qualifying experience within 10 years preceding application. Foreign-country equivalents also accepted.

Out-of-state CPAs with substantially equivalent qualifications may practice without a MN license if they hold a valid CPA certificate in another state, have a bachelor's degree or higher with accounting concentration, and have passed the Uniform CPA Examination. They are subject to board jurisdiction and must comply with MN statutes and rules.

Out-of-state CPAs with substantially equivalent qualifications may practice without obtaining a MO license; those establishing principal place of business in MO must obtain a MO license and may use NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service. Foreign designation holders may also obtain a license if reciprocal provisions are met.

The other state must grant similar privileges to Mississippi CPAs. The reciprocal license does not allow practice as a CPA unless the holder meets Mississippi Board requirements. Additionally, individuals whose principal place of business is not in MS who hold a valid CPA license from a substantially equivalent state may exercise practice privileges without obtaining a MS license.

Out-of-state CPAs whose home state has been verified as substantially equivalent by NASBA NQAS may practice with a practice privilege without notice, fee, or submission. Those not from verified-equivalent states may individually obtain NASBA verification of substantial equivalency. Firms employing such persons performing attest or compilations for Montana clients must be registered under 37-50-335.

Holder of valid and unrevoked CPA certificate from another state/territory/DC with substantially equivalent requirements; granting state must grant same privileges to NC certificate holders; Board may grant temporary permits pending qualification

Reciprocity available via substantial equivalency standard verified by NASBA national qualification appraisal service, or for non-substantially-equivalent states: passed uniform CPA exam, four years experience, and continuing education compliance.

Board may waive exam and issue reciprocal certificate to out-of-state CPA holders. Mandatory waiver (of exam and education) if applicant holds valid out-of-state CPA certificate, meets current Nebraska requirements, and has at least 4 years of experience within the preceding 10 years.

Substantial equivalency: education, examination, and experience requirements of another jurisdiction must be comparable to or exceed those in the Uniform Accountancy Act, or the individual CPA's qualifications must be comparable to or exceed UAA requirements.

Applicant must hold valid, unrevoked out-of-state CPA license from a jurisdiction with substantially equivalent education, experience, and examination requirements. Alternatively, out-of-state CPAs with substantially equivalent qualifications (as verified by NASBA) may practice in NJ without obtaining a license under the practice privilege provisions.

Applicant must have passed the qualifying exam with grades that would have been passing in NM, met experience requirements within the last 10 years, and if certificate was issued more than 4 years prior, fulfilled CPE requirements. Alternatively, a board-approved national qualification appraisal service may confirm substantial equivalency.

Applicant must hold a valid out-of-state CPA certificate, have passed a substantially equivalent exam with a passing grade, have at least 4 of 10 preceding years of experience while holding a CPA certificate, and meet Nevada's education requirements. For foreign-country CPAs, reciprocal privileges must exist and additional conditions apply.

Board of Regents may endorse an out-of-state license upon filing application, meeting education and experience requirements, passing examination, being at least 21, being of good moral character, and meeting citizenship/immigration status requirements. Additionally, practice privilege is available for CPAs licensed in states with substantially equivalent requirements who practice in another state as their principal place of business.

Out-of-state CPAs with substantially equivalent qualifications (valid foreign certificate, baccalaureate or higher degree, accounting concentration, passed all parts of the uniform CPA exam) may practice in Ohio without obtaining an Ohio CPA certificate and permit. Chapter 4796 reciprocity also applies.

Applicant must have passed a qualifying CPA examination with equivalent grades, and must meet current Oklahoma requirements, or met requirements on the date their original certificate was issued, or met candidate requirements at the time. Alternatively, NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service verification of substantial equivalency. Ethics exam required on or after July 1, 2005. CPE requirements must be met.

Applicant must be licensed in good standing as a CPA in another state, submit an application, pass the ethics exam, pay the fee, and provide evidence that either: (A) the other state's licensing requirements are substantially equivalent to Oregon's, or (B) the person has been practicing as a CPA for 4+ years within the last 10 years. Alternatively, holders of substantially equivalent out-of-state CPA licenses may practice in Oregon without obtaining an Oregon license under the practice privilege provisions of ORS 673.153.

Domestic reciprocity available without re-examination for holders of valid CPA certificates from other states who meet general qualifications, CE requirements, and experience requirements, or who have held a certificate and license for the immediately preceding five years. Foreign reciprocity also available under free trade agreements meeting education, examination, and experience standards substantially equivalent to Pennsylvania's.

Applicant must meet all current RI requirements at time of application and must have met all requirements applicable in RI at time of original issuance, or meet substantial equivalency standard under § 5-3.1-7(g). Out-of-state CPAs from substantially equivalent states may practice without obtaining a RI certificate or permit (practice privilege), subject to consent conditions.

Applicant must have passed the Uniform CPA Examination, hold an active certificate/license/permit from another US state, territory, DC, or IQAB-recognized foreign authority, be legally authorized to practice in that jurisdiction, and certify compliance with its CPE requirements.

Certificate issued to applicants from substantially equivalent states upon verification; also available to those not qualifying under substantial equivalency upon showing of passing exam grades, 4 years of experience, and CPE compliance.

Substantial equivalency: out-of-state CPA whose state has been verified as substantially equivalent may practice without notice or fee; those from non-verified states may obtain individual verification. Licensees must consent to board jurisdiction, comply with TN law, cease practice if home-state license lapses, and appoint home-state board as agent for service of process.

Applicant must hold a certificate or license from another state and either: (A) meet TX requirements except exam grades, (B) met TX requirements in effect when originally licensed, or (C) have at least 4 years of post-exam experience within 10 years of application; and must have met CPE requirements for 3 years preceding application.

Licensure by endorsement available for out-of-state CPA licensees. Applicant must show evidence of passing qualifying examinations and either meet Utah requirements applicable at time of original licensure, have 4 years of professional experience after passing the AICPA Uniform CPA Examination within the 10 years preceding application, or demonstrate substantial equivalency of education, examination, and experience to Utah requirements.

Applicant must disclose all states of licensure, provide documentation of good standing, disclose any violations, demonstrate substantially equivalent education, pass the CPA examination, and meet CPE and experience requirements as determined by the Board.

Licensure by endorsement requires either: (1) education, examination, and experience requirements substantially equal to Vermont's; or (2) five years of experience in the practice of public accountancy within the last 10 years plus fulfillment of applicable continuing education requirements.

Reciprocal state must make similar provision; applicant must meet CPE requirements, good character requirements, and either passed the exam with passing grades or has sufficient experience (3 years within 5 years or 5 years within 10 years). Board may accept NASBA substantial equivalency designation.
Applicant must hold a CPA certificate or license from another state or foreign country and establish substantial equivalence of qualifications required under s. 442.04.

Substantial equivalency: out-of-state certificate holders whose state has substantially equivalent CPA certification requirements, or who individually have substantially equivalent qualifications as verified by NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service, may practice without obtaining a WV certificate. Those seeking to establish principal place of business in WV must apply for a WV certificate.

Applicant must meet the substantial equivalency standard (150 semester hours, baccalaureate or higher degree, passing the uniform CPA exam, and 1 year experience). Alternatively, if not meeting substantial equivalency, applicant must have passed the uniform CPA exam and have 4 years of qualifying experience within the 10 years preceding application.
